about: The graph network's registered snapshots: immutable weights in gs://inkit-research-ml/models/<id>/model.pt (private: trained on others' puzzles), each with its card here. Experiments fork from a snapshot by id and register what they produce with `parent` set. Metrics are from the run's own report (research-cross-type.md section given); 'human' is the human-made test set (graphs-human.jsonl), never trained on.

data.humanLabels: graphs-human-labels.jsonl, split train (2,669 puzzles, 244,188 states; 329 more held back to pick the epoch)

models.notes: The baseline fine-tuned on Janko's move labels (opus_human_tune.py): predicts people's next moves, not correct ones (86% of its top guesses on opus-human's 400 states are correct). docs/research-opus-human-moves.md, 'The two checks'.
Everything that helped so far, no human puzzles in training. The fork point for the cheap-solver loop (capability) and for human-likeness experiments. research-cross-type.md §14.
Structure as input at width 128, the old test only (before the human test set and the leakage fix). research-cross-type.md §11.
The learning curve's full-data point, no structure. research-cross-type.md §13.

models.notes: As human-tuned-2026-10-20, with GRAPH_RELATIONS=1 (load it with that set): a digit mark's number beside the others. Hidoku 56.5% against 10%. docs/research-opus-human-moves.md, 'Why Hidoku'.
